description:
FOUND s470bz (Opus, 2026-09-07) by tools/t/install-container.t leg (c), on its
FIRST run: root installs /opt/pcl, a normal user runs
`/opt/pcl/bin/pcl -e 'use List::Util qw(sum); print sum(1..3)'`, and SBCL dies

    Unhandled sb-int:simple-file-error ... Can't create directory /root/.cache
    ... #P"/root/.cache/common-lisp/sbcl-2.6.0-linux-x64/opt/pcldeps/quicklisp/quicklisp/package.fasl"

REPRODUCER WITHOUT A CONTAINER (this dev box, 2026-09-07):

    $ cat probe.lisp
    (require :asdf)
    (format t "xdg-cache-home=~a~%" (uiop:xdg-cache-home))
    (format t "user-cache=~a~%" (symbol-value (find-symbol "*USER-CACHE*" "ASDF")))
    (format t "translated=~a~%"
            (funcall (find-symbol "APPLY-OUTPUT-TRANSLATIONS" "ASDF") #p"/opt/x/y.lisp"))

    $ HOME=/tmp/other sbcl --noinform --non-interactive --load probe.lisp
    xdg-cache-home=/tmp/other/.cache/
    user-cache=/tmp/other/.cache/common-lisp/sbcl-2.6.0.debian-linux-x64/
    translated=/tmp/other/.cache/common-lisp/.../opt/x/y.lisp

    $ HOME=/tmp/other sbcl --core ~/.pcl-cache/core/pcl-<...>.core \
          --noinform --non-interactive --load probe.lisp
    xdg-cache-home=/tmp/other/.cache/          <-- correct, read at call time
    user-cache=/home/bernt/.cache/common-lisp/sbcl-2.6.0.debian-linux-x64/
    translated=/home/bernt/.cache/common-lisp/.../opt/x/y.lisp   <-- THE BUILDER'S

MECHANISM.  UIOP computes asdf:*user-cache* once and keeps it; ASDF normally
recomputes it on image restore through uiop's image-restore hooks, which run
when an image is dumped/started via uiop:dump-image / uiop:restore-image.  PCL
saves its cores with a bare `(sb-ext:save-lisp-and-die ... :executable nil)` â
tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm:237 (the per-user cached core) and tools/install-pcl:293
(the installed core) â so those hooks never run and the builder's paths stay.

WHO IT BITES.  Only a process that does ASDF work at RUN time.  PCL itself does
none: cl-ppcre is inside the core, the extensions are plain `load`s from the
tree, and a module fasl is compiled by compile-file into PCL's own cache, whose
directory has been a process fact since #1303.  It bites when a sysinit or
userinit does ASDF work â the ordinary way to make Quicklisp visible to every
user on a machine â which is exactly the shared-install shape a system-wide
`tools/install-pcl --prefix /opt/pcl` invites.  It also bites the same user
running under a different HOME.

THIS IS THE #1303 FAMILY, one layer out: a cache directory that must be a fact
of the RUNNING process was frozen when a core was SAVED.

CANDIDATE FIX (not taken here, and why).  An sb-ext:*init-hooks* entry in
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp that clears ASDF's configuration when ASDF is present:

    (push (lambda ()
            (let ((f (and (find-package "ASDF")
                          (find-symbol "CLEAR-OUTPUT-TRANSLATIONS" "ASDF"))))
              (when f (funcall f))))
          sb-ext:*init-hooks*)

Init hooks run before SBCL processes the sysinit (measured: the failing
backtrace's frame 41 is PROCESS-INIT-FILE inside TOPLEVEL-INIT, which is after
reinit), so the ordering works.  NOT DONE IN s470bz because it is a `cl/`
change and therefore owes the full sweep plus companion legs, and because
clearing ASDF's configuration on EVERY start has a cost that has to be measured
against Target A before it is imposed on every run â a re-scan of the source
registry is not free.  Measure first: time `pcl -e 1` with and without.

WHERE IT IS RECORDED MEANWHILE: tools/t/install-container.t's image writes an
/etc/sbclrc that loads Quicklisp only `(unless (find-package "QUICKLISP-CLIENT"))`,
with a comment naming this task.  That guard is what any /etc/sbclrc should say
â a core that already has Quicklisp must not re-enter ASDF â so the leg
measures the installation and not this bug.  Removing the guard is how to
reproduce it in the container again.
subject: a saved PCL core memoises the BUILDER's asdf:*user-cache*, so any ASDF work in another user's process targets a directory it cannot write â a shared install breaks
